stemMd:
The system of equations below has the solution $(x, y)$.

$$3x + 2y = 31$$
$$5x - 2y = 25$$

What is the value of $x + y$?
explanationMd:
The $y$ terms are $+2y$ and $-2y$, so adding the equations eliminates $y$ immediately — no rearranging needed.

$$(3x + 2y) + (5x - 2y) = 31 + 25$$
$$8x = 56$$
$$x = 7$$

Substitute $x = 7$ into the first equation:

$$3(7) + 2y = 31 \;\Rightarrow\; 21 + 2y = 31 \;\Rightarrow\; 2y = 10 \;\Rightarrow\; y = 5$$

So $x + y = 7 + 5 = 12$.

Check both equations, not just the one you substituted into: $3(7) + 2(5) = 31$ and $5(7) - 2(5) = 35 - 10 = 25$. Both hold.

Note what the question actually asks for. It wants $x + y$, not $x$ and not $y$ — reread the final line before you choose.

distractorRationale.a: This is $x - y = 7 - 5$. The signs in the system tempt you into subtracting the values at the end, but the question asks for their sum.
distractorRationale.b: This is the value of $y$ alone. It is correct as far as it goes, but the question asks for $x + y$, so the substitution step was never completed.
distractorRationale.c: This is the value of $x$ alone, obtained after the elimination step. Stopping here skips finding $y$ and skips the addition the question asks for.

accessibilityText: A system of two equations: three x plus two y equals thirty-one, and five x minus two y equals twenty-five. Find the value of x plus y.

provenance.notes: Original item. Numbers chosen so elimination is immediate and x, y, x+y and x-y are four distinct values.

independentSolve.workingNotes: Adding the equations eliminates y: 8x = 56, x = 7; then 21 + 2y = 31 gives y = 5, so x + y = 12. Options B and C are y and x individually.
